1661def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
1662    """Fit the development trees' bends; choose the prior; compare the seasons; print and save.
1663
1664    Args:
1665        argv: Command-line arguments; ``None`` reads ``sys.argv[1:]``.
1666
1667    Returns:
1668        The exit status: 0 on success, 1 if no development tree with winter clicks was found or an output file
1669        could not be written; with ``--typical``, that of :func:`typical_main`.
1670    """
1671    import argparse
1672    import json
1673    import os
1674    import time
1675    from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
1676    from pathlib import Path
1677
1678    from treeskel.guided_gt import load_clicks
1679    from treeskel.io import index_dataset
1680    from treeskel.segment import hand_mask, load_masks
1681    from treeskel.summer_gt import load_overlays
1682
1683    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m treeskel.bend3d", description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
1684    ap.add_argument("data_dirs", nargs="*", help="dataset folder(s)")
1685    ap.add_argument("--clicks", default="annotations/winter_clicks.json", help="the winter clicks")
1686    ap.add_argument("--mask-overlay", default="annotations/mask_overlay.json", help="the hand masks' line-up")
1687    ap.add_argument("--unet", default="docs/results/segment_lined_up_joined/predicted_masks.npz",
1688                    help="the named U-Net's development masks (5 folds)")
1689    ap.add_argument("--split", default="splits.json", help="its test rows are never loaded; its folds group rows")
1690    ap.add_argument("--out", default="docs/results/bend3d")
1691    ap.add_argument("--trees", nargs="+", help="only these trees (results go to outputs/bend3d_partial)")
1692    ap.add_argument("--jobs", type=int, default=os.cpu_count() or 1)
1693    ap.add_argument("--from-saved", metavar="DIR", help="re-summarise a saved run's cv.csv and trees.csv (no images)")
1694    ap.add_argument("--figure", default="docs/figures/bend3d.png", help="the summary figure ('' for none)")
1695    ap.add_argument("--profiles", nargs="+", metavar="TREE", help="also draw these trees' winter profiles")
1696    ap.add_argument("--profiles-figure", default="docs/figures/bend3d_profiles.png")
1697    ap.add_argument("--typical", action="store_true",
1698                    help="the typical winter shape as the prior's mean: learn it, and compare summer with it "
1699                         "(-> docs/results/bend3d_typical/, docs/figures/bend3d_typical.png)")
1700    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
1701    if args.typical:
1702        return typical_main(args)
1703
1704    split = json.loads(Path(args.split).read_text())
1705    fold_rows = split["fold_val_rows"]
1706    failed: list[str] = []
1707    if args.from_saved:                                  # only the summary again, from the saved rows
1708        out = Path(args.out if args.out != "docs/results/bend3d" else args.from_saved)
1709        cv_rows, rows = load_csv(Path(args.from_saved) / "cv.csv"), load_csv(Path(args.from_saved) / "trees.csv")
1710    else:
1711        if not args.data_dirs:
1712            ap.error("give the dataset folder(s), or --from-saved")
1713        test_rows = set(split["test_rows"])
1714        clicks = load_clicks(args.clicks)
1715        records = {t.tree_id: t for d in args.data_dirs for t in index_dataset(d).trees if t.row not in test_rows}
1716        ids = sorted(t for t in records if t in clicks and not clicks[t].skip and clicks[t].complete
1717                     and (not args.trees or t in args.trees))
1718        if not ids:
1719            print("No development-row trees with winter clicks found; nothing to measure.")
1720            return 1
1721        # A run on chosen trees goes to outputs/, so it never overwrites the committed full run.
1722        out = Path(args.out if not args.trees or args.out != "docs/results/bend3d" else "outputs/bend3d_partial")
1723        workers = max(1, min(args.jobs, len(ids)))
1724
1725        def run(fn, jobs, what):
1726            """Map ``fn`` over ``jobs`` in worker processes, printing progress."""
1727            t0, step, res = time.time(), max(1, min(25, len(jobs) // 10)), []
1728            with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers) as ex:
1729                for i, r in enumerate(ex.map(fn, jobs, chunksize=1), 1):
1730                    res.append(r)
1731                    if i % step == 0 or i == len(jobs):
1732                        el = time.time() - t0
1733                        print(f"  {what}: {i}/{len(jobs)} trees, {el:.0f} s elapsed, about "
1734                              f"{el / i * (len(jobs) - i):.0f} s left", flush=True)
1735            return res
1736
1737        # Phase 1: every tree's winter block cross-validation over the grid of priors.
1738        print(f"Phase 1: block cross-validation of the winter depth on {len(ids)} development trees "
1739              f"({len(GRID)} priors and the plane)...", flush=True)
1740        results = run(cv_tree, [(records[t], clicks[t]) for t in ids], "phase 1")
1741        cv_rows = cv_table(results)
1742        out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
1743        save_csv(out / "cv.csv", cv_rows)
1744        cv_rows = load_csv(out / "cv.csv")
1745        # The rule fixed before the run: the prior with the smallest pooled left-out error.
1746        params = params_of(choose(cv_rows))
1747        print(f"Chosen prior: {setting_key(params)}", flush=True)
1748
1749        # Phase 2: the chosen prior on every tree: winter (every camera setting), the hand mask, the U-Net's mask.
1750        overlays = load_overlays(args.mask_overlay)
1751        unet = load_masks(Path(args.unet)) if Path(args.unet).exists() else {}
1752        radii = {r["tree"]: r["radii"] for r in results}
1753        jobs = [(records[t], clicks[t], radii[t], hand_mask(records[t], overlays), unet.get(t), params) for t in ids]
1754        print(f"Phase 2: the chosen prior on {len(ids)} trees, winter and summer...", flush=True)
1755        rows = [r for rs in run(measure_tree, jobs, "phase 2") for r in rs]
1756        save_csv(out / "trees.csv", rows)
1757        rows = load_csv(out / "trees.csv")              # the report from the saved rows, so it reproduces
1758
1759        if args.profiles:
1760            panels = []
1761            for t in args.profiles:
1762                if t not in records or t not in clicks:
1763                    print(f"  {t}: not a development tree with clicks; no profile")
1764                    continue
1765                images, sk = winter_skeleton(records[t], clicks[t])
1766                try:
1767                    prep = prepare(sk["paths"], images["depth"], images["valid"], sk["radii"])
1768                except ValueError as e:
1769                    print(f"  {t}: {e}")
1770                    continue
1771                fit = fit_bends(prep, params)
1772                panels.append((f"{t} winter", prep, fit, posterior_sd(fit)))
1773            if panels:
1774                plot_profiles(panels, Path(args.profiles_figure), failed,
1775                              f"Winter depth along the branches and the fitted bends ({setting_key(params)})")
1776
1777    report = summarise(cv_rows, rows, fold_rows)
1778    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
1779    (out / "report.json").write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
1780    lines = report_lines(report)
1781    print("\n".join(lines))
1782    try:
1783        (out / "output.txt").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
1784    except OSError as e:
1785        failed.append(f"{out / 'output.txt'}: {e.strerror or e}")
1786    if args.figure:
1787        Path(args.figure).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
1788        plot_figure(cv_rows, rows, fold_rows, Path(args.figure), failed)
1789    print(f"\nSaved cv.csv, trees.csv, report.json and output.txt in {out}"
1790          + (f", and {args.figure}" if args.figure else ""))
1791    for f in failed:
1792        print(f"Could not write {f}")
1793    return 1 if failed else 0
1794

1796def run_parallel(fn, jobs: Sequence, what: str, workers: int) -> list:
1797    """Map ``fn`` over ``jobs`` in worker processes, printing progress, in the jobs' order.
1798
1799    Args:
1800        fn: A top-level function of one job.
1801        jobs: The jobs.
1802        what: What the progress lines call the step.
1803        workers: Most worker processes.
1804
1805    Returns:
1806        ``fn``'s results, in the order of ``jobs``.
1807    """
1808    import time
1809    from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
1810
1811    t0, step, res = time.time(), max(1, min(25, len(jobs) // 10)), []
1812    with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=max(1, min(workers, len(jobs)))) as ex:
1813        for i, r in enumerate(ex.map(fn, jobs, chunksize=1), 1):
1814            res.append(r)
1815            if i % step == 0 or i == len(jobs):
1816                el = time.time() - t0
1817                print(f"  {what}: {i}/{len(jobs)} trees, {el:.0f} s elapsed, about {el / i * (len(jobs) - i):.0f} s left",
1818                      flush=True)
1819    return res
1820
1821

1823"""Where ``--typical`` writes, and :mod:`treeskel.model3d` reads the typical shape (``typical_shape.json``)."""
1824
1825
1826def typical_main(args) -> int:
1827    """``--typical``: learn the typical winter shape and compare summer with it (development rows only).
1828
1829    Pass 1 fits every development tree's winter bends with the chosen prior (``docs/results/bend3d/report.json``)
1830    and samples them along each part; the typical shape is learnt from all trees and, for each fold, from the
1831    other folds' trees. Pass 2 fits summer (the lined-up hand mask and the U-Net's mask) with the plane and with
1832    the out-of-fold typical shape as the prior's mean. The rule (:data:`TYPICAL_RULE`) decides whether
1833    :mod:`treeskel.model3d` uses the shape.
1834
1835    Args:
1836        args: The parsed command line of :func:`main`.
1837
1838    Returns:
1839        The exit status: 0 on success, 1 if no development tree with winter clicks was found or an output file
1840        could not be written, 2 if neither the dataset folders nor ``--from-saved`` was given.
1841    """
1842    import json
1843    from pathlib import Path
1844
1845    from treeskel.guided_gt import load_clicks
1846    from treeskel.io import index_dataset
1847    from treeskel.segment import hand_mask, load_masks
1848    from treeskel.summer_gt import load_overlays
1849
1850    out = Path(TYPICAL_OUT if args.out == "docs/results/bend3d" else args.out)
1851    figure = "docs/figures/bend3d_typical.png" if args.figure == "docs/figures/bend3d.png" else args.figure
1852    split = json.loads(Path(args.split).read_text())
1853    fold_rows = split["fold_val_rows"]
1854    failed: list[str] = []
1855    if args.from_saved:
1856        rows = load_csv(Path(args.from_saved) / "trees.csv")
1857        shapes = json.loads((Path(args.from_saved) / "typical_shape.json").read_text())
1858        out = Path(args.out if args.out != "docs/results/bend3d" else args.from_saved)
1859    else:
1860        if not args.data_dirs:
1861            print("give the dataset folder(s), or --from-saved")
1862            return 2
1863        chosen = Path("docs/results/bend3d/report.json")
1864        params = params_of(json.loads(chosen.read_text())["chosen"]) if chosen.exists() else BendParams()
1865        clicks = load_clicks(args.clicks)
1866        records = {t.tree_id: t for d in args.data_dirs for t in index_dataset(d).trees
1867                   if t.row not in set(split["test_rows"])}
1868        ids = sorted(t for t in records if t in clicks and not clicks[t].skip and clicks[t].complete
1869                     and (not args.trees or t in args.trees))
1870        if not ids:
1871            print("No development-row trees with winter clicks found; nothing to measure.")
1872            return 1
1873        if args.trees and args.out == "docs/results/bend3d":
1874            out = Path("outputs/bend3d_typical_partial")     # a run on chosen trees never overwrites the full run
1875        print(f"Pass 1: winter bends ({setting_key(params)}) of {len(ids)} development trees...", flush=True)
1876        winter = run_parallel(typical_winter, [(records[t], clicks[t], params) for t in ids], "pass 1", args.jobs)
1877        shapes = fold_shapes(winter, fold_rows)
1878        # Each tree's summer is fitted with the shape learnt without its own fold.
1879        overlays = load_overlays(args.mask_overlay)
1880        unet = load_masks(Path(args.unet)) if Path(args.unet).exists() else {}
1881        jobs = [(records[t], hand_mask(records[t], overlays), unet.get(t), params,
1882                 shapes["folds"][fold_of(records[t].row, fold_rows)]) for t in ids]
1883        print(f"Pass 2: summer with the plane and with the typical shape as the prior's mean...", flush=True)
1884        rows = [{"tree": w["tree"], "row": w["row"], "source": "winter", "setting": "main", "model": "bent",
1885                 "error": w["error"], **(w["measures"] or {})} for w in winter]
1886        rows += [r for rs in run_parallel(typical_summer, jobs, "pass 2", args.jobs) for r in rs]
1887        out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
1888        save_csv(out / "trees.csv", rows)
1889        rows = load_csv(out / "trees.csv")
1890        shapes = {**shapes, "prior": setting_key(params), "min_trees": MIN_TREES,
1891                  "trees": len([w for w in winter if w["profiles"] is not None])}
1892        (out / "typical_shape.json").write_text(json.dumps(shapes, indent=1))
1893        np.savez_compressed(out / "profiles.npz", ids=np.array([w["tree"] for w in winter if w["profiles"] is not None]),
1894                            **{p: np.array([w["profiles"][p] for w in winter if w["profiles"] is not None])
1895                               for p in PARTS}, **{f"stations_{p}": STATIONS[p] for p in PARTS})
1896    report = summarise_typical(rows, shapes)
1897    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
1898    (out / "report.json").write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
1899    lines = typical_lines(report)
1900    print("\n".join(lines))
1901    try:
1902        (out / "output.txt").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
1903    except OSError as e:
1904        failed.append(f"{out / 'output.txt'}: {e.strerror or e}")
1905    if figure:
1906        Path(figure).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
1907        plot_typical(report, Path(figure), failed)
1908    print(f"\nSaved trees.csv, typical_shape.json, profiles.npz, report.json and output.txt in {out}"
1909          + (f", and {figure}" if figure else ""))
1910    for f in failed:
1911        print(f"Could not write {f}")
1912    return 1 if failed else 0
1913

1916    raise SystemExit(main())
FORK_VALUE = 132.9156223893066

The depth value of the median development tree's winter fork (about 132.9), which treeskel.depth3d.METRES_PER_UNIT puts at treeskel.depth3d.DISTANCE_M.

RIDGE_GAP = 6

A summer branch's sides are read this many px beyond its edge (depth reaches about 2 px past an edge).

RIDGE_CONTRAST = 4.0

Both sides must read at least this many depth units (about 5 cm) farther for a summer reading to count.

CORR_PX = 7.0

Each depth reading along a path counts as Δs / CORR_PX independent ones: it is the median of a 3 px disc (treeskel.tree3d.depth_along()), 7 px across, so neighbouring readings share most of their pixels.

BLOCK_PX = 40

Length of the blocks block_cv() leaves out (px along the branch; about 13 cm at 2 m).

BUFFER_PX = 10

Readings this many px either side of a left-out block are left out too, but not scored.

MAX_TURN = 60.0

A plane turned more than this (degrees) from facing the camera is a failed fit (prepare() refuses it): the 449 winter planes turn a median 4.4°, and treeskel.tree3d.TURNED lists those past 20°.

GRID = ((0.01, 0.05), (0.01, 0.1), (0.01, 0.2), (0.01, 0.4), (0.02, 0.05), (0.02, 0.1), (0.02, 0.2), (0.02, 0.4), (0.04, 0.05), (0.04, 0.1), (0.04, 0.2), (0.04, 0.4), (0.08, 0.05), (0.08, 0.1), (0.08, 0.2), (0.08, 0.4), (0.16, 0.05), (0.16, 0.1), (0.16, 0.2), (0.16, 0.4))

The priors block_cv() tries: (spread, length) in metres (τ and L), besides the plane (τ = 0).

def per_unit(camera: treeskel.depth3d.Camera) -> float: 
109def per_unit(camera: Camera) -> float:
110    """Metres per depth unit for a camera setting: the median development fork at 2.0 m.
111
112    The same scale as :func:`treeskel.tree3d.scales` (to 0.2%), without needing every tree.
113
114    Args:
115        camera: The depth map's zero and the focal length.
116
117    Returns:
118        Metres per depth unit.
119
120    Example:
121        >>> round(per_unit(Camera()), 5)
122        0.01197
123    """
124    return DISTANCE_M / (camera.zero - FORK_VALUE)

Metres per depth unit for a camera setting: the median development fork at 2.0 m.

The same scale as treeskel.tree3d.scales() (to 0.2%), without needing every tree.

Arguments:
  • camera: The depth map's zero and the focal length.

Example:

def axis_distance( values: numpy.ndarray, radii_px: numpy.ndarray, camera: treeskel.depth3d.Camera) -> numpy.ndarray: 
160def axis_distance(values: np.ndarray, radii_px: np.ndarray, camera: Camera) -> np.ndarray:
161    """Distance (units, along the optical axis) to a branch's axis, from the depth of its near surface.
162
163    The axis lies one radius behind the surface; a radius of ``r`` px at distance ``Z`` is ``r Z / f``.
164
165    Args:
166        values: Depth units ``zero − v`` of the near surface (distance in units).
167        radii_px: The branch's radius at each point (photo px).
168        camera: The camera's focal length.
169
170    Returns:
171        The distances to the axis, in the same units as ``values``.
172
173    Example:
174        >>> axis_distance(np.array([100.0]), np.array([10.0]), Camera(zero=300.0, focal=500.0)).tolist()
175        [204.0]
176    """
177    z = camera.distance(values)
178    return z * (1.0 + np.asarray(radii_px, float) / camera.focal)

def ridge_contrast( depth: numpy.ndarray, valid: numpy.ndarray, path: numpy.ndarray, radii_px: numpy.ndarray, gap: float = 6) -> numpy.ndarray: 
181def ridge_contrast(depth: np.ndarray, valid: np.ndarray, path: np.ndarray, radii_px: np.ndarray,
182                   gap: float = RIDGE_GAP) -> np.ndarray:
183    """How much farther than a branch its two sides read (depth units; the smaller of the two sides).
184
185    Each side is read ``radius + gap`` px out along the path's normal (median within 2 px); a side with no
186    reading counts as infinitely far. NaN where the branch itself has no reading.
187
188    Args:
189        depth: ``(480, 640)`` uint8 depth.
190        valid: Boolean mask of its readings.
191        path: ``(N, 2)`` ``(row, col)`` points along the branch.
192        radii_px: The branch's radius at each point (px).
193        gap: How far beyond the radius each side is read (px).
194
195    Returns:
196        ``(N,)`` contrasts in depth units (``inf`` if neither side has a reading, NaN where the branch has
197        none).
198    """
199    p = np.asarray(path, float).reshape(-1, 2)
200    normals = path_normals(np.rint(p).astype(int), 6)
201    centre = depth_along(depth, valid, p)
202    out = np.full(len(p), np.inf)
203    for sign in (-1.0, 1.0):
204        side = p + sign * (np.asarray(radii_px, float) + gap)[:, None] * normals
205        v = depth_along(depth, valid, side, radius=2, min_valid=3)
206        out = np.minimum(out, np.where(np.isnan(v), np.inf, centre - v))
207    out[np.isnan(centre)] = np.nan
208    return out

How much farther than a branch its two sides read (depth units; the smaller of the two sides).

Each side is read radius + gap px out along the path's normal (median within 2 px); a side with no reading counts as infinitely far. NaN where the branch itself has no reading.

Arguments:
  • depth: (480, 640) uint8 depth.
  • valid: Boolean mask of its readings.
  • path: (N, 2) (row, col) points along the branch.
  • radii_px: The branch's radius at each point (px).
  • gap: How far beyond the radius each side is read (px).
Returns:

(N,) contrasts in depth units (inf if neither side has a reading, NaN where the branch has none).

217    """One tree's skeleton and readings, ready to fit: the parts as chains of nodes from the fork.
218
219    Node 0 is the fork; each part's other points follow it outwards (the trunk reversed, so towards the
220    root). Arrays are per node unless named per part.

222    Attributes:
223        paths: Each part's ``(row, col)`` photo points, in the caller's order (trunk root to fork).
224        nodes: Per part, the node of each of its points (same order as ``paths``).
225        chains: Per part, its nodes from the fork outwards (starting with 0).
226        rays: ``(N, 3)`` ray directions ``(x, y, 1)``.
227        z_axis: Distance to the branch's axis (m) where read, else NaN.
228        anchor: Readings that count (all readings in winter; ridges in summer).
229        cell_px: Each node's share of its path's length (px), for its readings' weight.
230        plane: :func:`treeskel.tree3d.fit_plane` through every reading's axis point (m).
231        z_plane: The plane's distance along each ray (m).
232        s: Per part, the length along the chain on the plane (m), from the fork.
233        s_px: Per part, the length along the chain in the photo (px), from the fork.
234        per_unit: Metres per depth unit.
235    """
236
237    paths: dict
238    nodes: dict
239    chains: dict
240    rays: np.ndarray
241    z_axis: np.ndarray
242    anchor: np.ndarray
243    cell_px: np.ndarray
244    plane: dict

246    s: dict
247    s_px: dict

251    def d(self) -> np.ndarray:
252        """The readings' distance behind the plane along their rays (m), NaN where none count."""
253        return np.where(self.anchor, self.z_axis - self.z_plane, np.nan)

s_px: dict

The readings' distance behind the plane along their rays (m), NaN where none count.

def prepare( paths: dict, depth: numpy.ndarray, valid: numpy.ndarray, radii: dict, camera: treeskel.depth3d.Camera = Camera(zero=300.0, focal=616.0, centre=(240.0, 320.0)), ridge: bool = False, scale: float | None = None) -> Prepared: 
256def prepare(paths: dict, depth: np.ndarray, valid: np.ndarray, radii: dict, camera: Camera = Camera(),
257            ridge: bool = False, scale: float | None = None) -> Prepared:
258    """One tree's skeleton with its depth, plane and chains.
259
260    Args:
261        paths: ``{"trunk", "left", "right"}`` ``(N, 2)`` ``(row, col)`` photo points: the trunk from the root
262            to the fork, each leader from the fork to its tip.
263        depth: The photo's ``(480, 640)`` uint8 depth.
264        valid: Boolean mask of the depth's readings.
265        radii: Each part's radius at each point (photo px).
266        camera: The depth map and camera.
267        ridge: Count only the readings where the branch is a depth ridge (:func:`ridge_contrast`; summer).
268        scale: Metres per unit (default :func:`per_unit` of ``camera``).
269
270    Returns:
271        The :class:`Prepared` tree.
272
273    Raises:
274        ValueError: If fewer than 20 points have depth (no plane).
275    """
276    pu = per_unit(camera) if scale is None else scale
277    paths = {p: np.asarray(paths[p], float).reshape(-1, 2) for p in PARTS}
278    fork = paths["trunk"][-1]
279    # The chains from the fork outwards; a leader's first point is the fork itself when it repeats it.
280    own = {"trunk": paths["trunk"][::-1][1:]}
281    for p in ("left", "right"):
282        own[p] = paths[p][1:] if len(paths[p]) and np.allclose(paths[p][0], fork) else paths[p]
283    rc = np.concatenate([fork[None], *(own[p] for p in PARTS)])
284    rad = np.concatenate([np.asarray(radii["trunk"], float)[-1:],
285                          *(np.asarray(radii[p], float)[::-1][1:] if p == "trunk"
286                            else np.asarray(radii[p], float)[len(radii[p]) - len(own[p]):] for p in PARTS)])
287    chains, nodes, k = {}, {}, 1
288    for p in PARTS:
289        idx = np.arange(k, k + len(own[p]))
290        chains[p] = np.r_[0, idx]
291        k += len(own[p])
292        if p == "trunk":
293            nodes[p] = chains[p][::-1]                          # root ... fork
294        else:
295            nodes[p] = chains[p] if len(paths[p]) > len(own[p]) else idx
296    values = depth_along(depth, valid, rc)
297    z_axis = axis_distance(values, rad, camera) * pu
298    read = np.isfinite(z_axis)
299    if read.sum() < 20:
300        raise ValueError(f"only {int(read.sum())} skeleton points have depth: no plane")
301    anchor = read.copy()
302    if ridge:
303        anchor &= ridge_contrast(depth, valid, rc, rad) >= RIDGE_CONTRAST
304    rays = camera.rays(rc)
305    plane = fit_plane(rays[read] * z_axis[read, None])
306    facing = float(np.degrees(np.arccos(np.clip(-plane["normal"][2], -1, 1))))
307    if facing > MAX_TURN:
308        # Rays nearly along the plane would put the skeleton metres away: the fit has failed.
309        raise ValueError(f"the tree's plane is turned {facing:.0f} degrees from the camera: a failed fit")
310    z_plane = on_plane(rays, plane)[:, 2]
311    on = rays * z_plane[:, None]
312    s, s_px = {}, {}
313    cell_px = np.zeros(len(rc))
314    for p in PARTS:
315        c = chains[p]
316        s[p] = np.r_[0.0, np.cumsum(np.linalg.norm(np.diff(on[c], axis=0), axis=1))]
317        steps = np.linalg.norm(np.diff(rc[c], axis=0), axis=1)
318        s_px[p] = np.r_[0.0, np.cumsum(steps)]
319        half = np.r_[0.0, steps / 2] + np.r_[steps / 2, 0.0]   # half of each neighbouring step
320        cell_px[c] += half
321    return Prepared(paths=paths, nodes=nodes, chains=chains, rays=rays, z_axis=z_axis, anchor=anchor,
322                    cell_px=cell_px, plane=plane, z_plane=z_plane, s=s, s_px=s_px, per_unit=pu)

One tree's skeleton with its depth, plane and chains.

Arguments:
  • paths: {"trunk", "left", "right"} (N, 2) (row, col) photo points: the trunk from the root to the fork, each leader from the fork to its tip.
  • depth: The photo's (480, 640) uint8 depth.
  • valid: Boolean mask of the depth's readings.
  • radii: Each part's radius at each point (photo px).
  • camera: The depth map and camera.
  • ridge: Count only the readings where the branch is a depth ridge (ridge_contrast(); summer).
  • scale: Metres per unit (default per_unit() of camera).
Returns:

The Prepared tree.

Raises:

def prior_terms( prep: Prepared) -> tuple[scipy.sparse._csc.csc_matrix, scipy.sparse._csc.csc_matrix]: 
325def prior_terms(prep: Prepared) -> tuple[sparse.csc_matrix, sparse.csc_matrix]:
326    """The prior's two parts on the chains' nodes: ``(mass, curvature)``.
327
328    ``hᵀ mass h ≈ ∫ h² ds`` and ``hᵀ curvature h ≈ ∫ (d²h/ds²)² ds``, summed over the three chains, with
329    the second differences taken within each chain (each may kink at the fork).
330
331    Args:
332        prep: The prepared tree.
333
334    Returns:
335        ``(mass, curvature)``, sparse square matrices over the nodes.
336    """
337    n = len(prep.z_axis)
338    mass = np.zeros(n)
339    rows, cols, vals = [], [], []
340    r = 0
341    for p in PARTS:
342        c, s = prep.chains[p], prep.s[p]
343        ds = np.maximum(np.diff(s), 1e-4)
344        mass[c] += np.r_[0.0, ds / 2] + np.r_[ds / 2, 0.0]
345        for j in range(1, len(c) - 1):
346            a, b = ds[j - 1], ds[j]
347            w = np.sqrt((a + b) / 2)
348            rows += [r, r, r]
349            cols += [c[j - 1], c[j], c[j + 1]]
350            vals += [w * 2 / (a * (a + b)), -w * 2 / (a * b), w * 2 / (b * (a + b))]
351            r += 1
352    g = sparse.csr_matrix((vals, (rows, cols)), shape=(r, n))
353    return sparse.diags(np.maximum(mass, 1e-6)).tocsc(), (g.T @ g).tocsc()

The prior's two parts on the chains' nodes: (mass, curvature).

hᵀ mass h ≈ ∫ h² ds and hᵀ curvature h ≈ ∫ (d²h/ds²)² ds, summed over the three chains, with the second differences taken within each chain (each may kink at the fork).

Arguments:
  • prep: The prepared tree.
Returns:

(mass, curvature), sparse square matrices over the nodes.

def precision( terms: tuple, params: BendParams) -> scipy.sparse._csc.csc_matrix: 
360def precision(terms: tuple, params: BendParams) -> sparse.csc_matrix:
361    """The prior's precision matrix for ``spread`` τ and ``length`` L: ``(mass + L⁴ curvature) / (2√2 τ² L)``.
362
363    The marginal standard deviation of a long chain under it is τ.
364
365    Args:
366        terms: ``(mass, curvature)`` from :func:`prior_terms`.
367        params: The prior's spread τ and length L (m).
368
369    Returns:
370        The sparse precision matrix.
371    """
372    mass, curv = terms
373    c = 1.0 / (2 * np.sqrt(2) * params.spread ** 2 * params.length)
374    return (c * (mass + params.length ** 4 * curv)).tocsc()

The prior's precision matrix for spread τ and length L: (mass + L⁴ curvature) / (2√2 τ² L).

The marginal standard deviation of a long chain under it is τ.

Arguments:
  • terms: (mass, curvature) from prior_terms().
  • params: The prior's spread τ and length L (m).
Returns:

The sparse precision matrix.

def fit_bends( prep: Prepared, params: BendParams = BendParams(spread=0.02, length=0.2, huber=1.345, tukey=4.685, iters=30, corr_px=7.0, min_noise=0.003, uncertain=0.5), d: numpy.ndarray | None = None, hold: numpy.ndarray | None = None, terms: tuple | None = None, mean: numpy.ndarray | None = None) -> dict: 
381def fit_bends(prep: Prepared, params: BendParams = BendParams(), d: np.ndarray | None = None,
382              hold: np.ndarray | None = None, terms: tuple | None = None, mean: np.ndarray | None = None) -> dict:
383    """The bends ``h`` (m behind the plane, along each ray) at every node, fitted robustly.
384
385    Solves ``(Q + W/σ²) h = W d/σ² + Q m`` with ``Q`` the prior's :func:`precision`, ``m`` its mean (the
386    plane, 0, unless ``mean`` is given), ``d`` the readings' distance behind the plane and ``W`` each
387    reading's weight (its robust weight times ``cell_px / corr_px``). Huber weights with the noise ``σ``
388    re-estimated each round, then Tukey's biweight with ``σ`` fixed.
389
390    Args:
391        prep: The tree (:func:`prepare`).
392        params: The prior and the robust fit; ``spread`` 0 gives the plane (``h`` = 0).
393        d: Readings behind the plane to use instead of ``prep.d`` (e.g. against a refitted plane).
394        hold: Nodes whose readings are left out.
395        terms: :func:`prior_terms`, to reuse across fits.
396        mean: The prior's mean at each node (m behind the plane), e.g. the typical winter shape
397            (:func:`prior_mean`); where nothing is read the bends follow it instead of the plane.
398
399    Returns:
400        ``{"h", "weights", "sigma", "observed", "system"}``: ``system`` is the final ``Q + W/σ²`` (for
401        :func:`posterior_sd`), None for the plane.
402    """
403    d = prep.d if d is None else d
404    obs = np.isfinite(d) & (True if hold is None else ~hold)
405    n = len(d)
406    if params.spread <= 0:
407        return {"h": np.zeros(n), "weights": obs.astype(float), "sigma": float("nan"), "observed": obs,
408                "system": None}
409    q = precision(terms or prior_terms(prep), params)
410    m = np.zeros(n) if mean is None else np.asarray(mean, float)
411    if obs.sum() == 0:                                  # nothing seen: the prior alone, its mean and its spread
412        return {"h": m.copy(), "weights": np.zeros(n), "sigma": float("nan"), "observed": obs, "system": q}
413    y = np.where(obs, d, 0.0)
414    cell = prep.cell_px / params.corr_px
415    sigma = max(_robust_scale((d - m)[obs]), params.min_noise)
416    w = obs.astype(float)
417    h = m.copy()
418    qm = q @ m
419
420    def solve(weights, s):
421        """The bends for these readings' weights and noise level, and the system solved."""
422        a = (q + sparse.diags(cell * weights / s ** 2)).tocsc()
423        return spsolve(a, cell * weights * y / s ** 2 + qm), a
424
425    a = None
426    # Huber: bounded influence, the noise level from the residuals each round.
427    for _ in range(params.iters):
428        h_new, a = solve(w, sigma)
429        r = np.where(obs, d - h_new, 0.0)
430        sigma = max(_robust_scale(r[obs]), params.min_noise)
431        w = np.where(obs, np.minimum(1.0, params.huber * sigma / np.maximum(np.abs(r), 1e-12)), 0.0)
432        done = np.max(np.abs(h_new - h)) < 1e-5
433        h = h_new
434        if done:
435            break
436    # Tukey's biweight from there, with the noise level fixed: far readings get no weight at all.
437    for _ in range(params.iters):
438        r = np.where(obs, d - h, 0.0)
439        u = r / (params.tukey * sigma)
440        w = np.where(obs & (np.abs(u) < 1), (1 - u ** 2) ** 2, 0.0)
441        h_new, a = solve(w, sigma)
442        done = np.max(np.abs(h_new - h)) < 1e-5
443        h = h_new
444        if done:
445            break
446    return {"h": h, "weights": w, "sigma": sigma, "observed": obs, "system": a}

The bends h (m behind the plane, along each ray) at every node, fitted robustly.

Solves (Q + W/σ²) h = W d/σ² + Q m with Q the prior's precision(), m its mean (the plane, 0, unless mean is given), d the readings' distance behind the plane and W each reading's weight (its robust weight times cell_px / corr_px). Huber weights with the noise σ re-estimated each round, then Tukey's biweight with σ fixed.

Arguments:
  • prep: The tree (prepare()).
  • params: The prior and the robust fit; spread 0 gives the plane (h = 0).
  • d: Readings behind the plane to use instead of prep.d (e.g. against a refitted plane).
  • hold: Nodes whose readings are left out.
  • terms: prior_terms(), to reuse across fits.
  • mean: The prior's mean at each node (m behind the plane), e.g. the typical winter shape (prior_mean()); where nothing is read the bends follow it instead of the plane.
Returns:

{"h", "weights", "sigma", "observed", "system"}: system is the final Q + W/σ² (for posterior_sd()), None for the plane.

def posterior_sd(fit: dict) -> numpy.ndarray: 
449def posterior_sd(fit: dict) -> np.ndarray:
450    """The posterior standard deviation of each node's bend (m), with the weights and noise as fitted.
451
452    It treats the prior, the noise and the plane as known, so it is a lower bound; 0 for the plane.
453
454    Args:
455        fit: A fit from :func:`fit_bends`.
456
457    Returns:
458        The standard deviation per node (m); zeros for the plane.
459    """
460    a = fit["system"]
461    n = len(fit["h"])
462    if a is None:
463        return np.zeros(n)
464    if n <= 4000:
465        return np.sqrt(np.clip(np.diag(np.linalg.inv(a.toarray())), 0, None))
466    lu = splu(a.tocsc())
467    return np.sqrt(np.clip([lu.solve(np.eye(1, n, i).ravel())[i] for i in range(n)], 0, None))

Returns:

The standard deviation per node (m); zeros for the plane.

483def behind_plane(prep: Prepared, points: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
484    """Signed distance of 3D points behind the tree's plane (m; positive = farther from the camera).

def profile( prep: Prepared, h: numpy.ndarray, part: str, stations: numpy.ndarray | None = None) -> numpy.ndarray: 
510def profile(prep: Prepared, h: np.ndarray, part: str, stations: np.ndarray | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
511    """One part's bend (m behind the plane) at the stations, NaN beyond the part's end in view.
512
513    Args:
514        prep: The prepared tree.
515        h: Each node's bend behind the plane (m).
516        part: ``"trunk"``, ``"left"`` or ``"right"``.
517        stations: Distances from the fork along the part (m); the part's :data:`STATIONS` by default.
518
519    Returns:
520        The bend at each station (m), NaN beyond the part's end.
521
522    Example:
523        >>> class P: chains = {"left": np.array([0, 1, 2])}; s = {"left": np.array([0.0, 0.1, 0.2])}
524        >>> profile(P, np.array([0.0, 0.01, 0.03]), "left", np.array([0.0, 0.15, 0.3])).round(3).tolist()
525        [0.0, 0.02, nan]
526    """
527    st = STATIONS[part] if stations is None else np.asarray(stations, float)
528    return np.interp(st, prep.s[part], np.asarray(h, float)[prep.chains[part]], right=np.nan)

def typical_shape(profiles: Sequence[dict], min_trees: int = 20) -> dict: 
531def typical_shape(profiles: Sequence[dict], min_trees: int = MIN_TREES) -> dict:
532    """The typical bend of each part: the median over trees of their winter profiles (:func:`profile`).
533
534    Each part's stations end before the first one fewer than ``min_trees`` trees reach. The three parts
535    share the fork, so their first value is set to the median fork bend.
536
537    Args:
538        profiles: Per tree, ``{part: values at STATIONS[part]}``.
539        min_trees: Fewest trees a station must have.
540
541    Returns:
542        ``{part: {"stations": [...], "bend": [...], "q1": [...], "q3": [...], "n": [...]}}`` in metres.
543    """
544    out = {}
545    for part in PARTS:
546        a = np.array([p[part] for p in profiles], float).reshape(-1, len(STATIONS[part]))
547        n = np.isfinite(a).sum(0)
548        keep = int(np.argmax(n < min_trees)) if np.any(n < min_trees) else len(n)
549        a = a[:, :keep]
550        out[part] = {"stations": STATIONS[part][:keep].tolist(),
551                     "bend": np.nanmedian(a, 0).tolist() if keep else [],
552                     "q1": np.nanpercentile(a, 25, 0).tolist() if keep else [],
553                     "q3": np.nanpercentile(a, 75, 0).tolist() if keep else [],
554                     "n": n[:keep].astype(int).tolist()}
555    fork = [np.array([p[part][0] for p in profiles], float) for part in PARTS]
556    f = float(np.nanmedian(np.concatenate(fork))) if len(profiles) else 0.0
557    for part in PARTS:
558        if out[part]["bend"]:
559            out[part]["bend"][0] = f
560    return out

The typical bend of each part: the median over trees of their winter profiles (profile()).

Each part's stations end before the first one fewer than min_trees trees reach. The three parts share the fork, so their first value is set to the median fork bend.

Arguments:
  • profiles: Per tree, {part: values at STATIONS[part]}.
  • min_trees: Fewest trees a station must have.
Returns:

{part: {"stations": [...], "bend": [...], "q1": [...], "q3": [...], "n": [...]}} in metres.

def prior_mean(prep: Prepared, shape: dict) -> numpy.ndarray: 
563def prior_mean(prep: Prepared, shape: dict) -> np.ndarray:
564    """The typical shape at each node of a tree (m behind its plane): each part's profile at the node's
565    distance from the fork, holding its last value beyond the stations it covers.
566
567    Args:
568        prep: The prepared tree.
569        shape: The typical shape, from :func:`typical_shape`.
570
571    Returns:
572        The prior's mean bend per node (m).
573    """
574    m = np.zeros(len(prep.z_axis))
575    for part in PARTS:
576        st, b = shape[part]["stations"], shape[part]["bend"]
577        if len(st):
578            m[prep.chains[part]] = np.interp(prep.s[part], st, b)
579    firsts = [shape[p]["bend"][0] for p in PARTS if len(shape[p]["bend"])]
580    m[0] = float(np.mean(firsts)) if firsts else 0.0
581    return m

The typical shape at each node of a tree (m behind its plane): each part's profile at the node's distance from the fork, holding its last value beyond the stations it covers.

Arguments:
  • prep: The prepared tree.
  • shape: The typical shape, from typical_shape().
Returns:

The prior's mean bend per node (m).

588def setting_key(params: BendParams) -> str:

def blocks( prep: Prepared, block_px: float = 40, buffer_px: float = 10) -> list[tuple]: 
600def blocks(prep: Prepared, block_px: float = BLOCK_PX, buffer_px: float = BUFFER_PX) -> list[tuple]:
601    """The left-out blocks: ``(part, scored, removed)`` node masks.
602
603    Each part is cut into blocks of ``block_px`` px from the fork outwards (the fork belongs to the trunk's
604    first block). A block's readings and those within ``buffer_px`` px of it are removed from the fit; only
605    the block's own are scored. Near the fork the buffer reaches into the other parts.
606
607    Args:
608        prep: The prepared tree.
609        block_px: Block length along the part (px).
610        buffer_px: Readings this close to a block are left out of its fit too (px).
611
612    Returns:
613        ``(part, scored, removed)`` per block: the part's name and two boolean node masks.
614    """
615    n = len(prep.z_axis)
616    out = []
617    for p in PARTS:
618        c, s = prep.chains[p], prep.s_px[p]
619        own = np.ones(len(c), bool) if p == "trunk" else np.r_[False, np.ones(len(c) - 1, bool)]
620        for k in range(int(s[-1] // block_px) + 1):              # the last block holds the chain's end
621            lo, hi = k * block_px, (k + 1) * block_px
622            scored, removed = np.zeros(n, bool), np.zeros(n, bool)
623            scored[c[own & (s >= lo) & (s < hi)]] = True
624            removed[c[(s >= lo - buffer_px) & (s < hi + buffer_px)]] = True
625            if lo - buffer_px < 0:                          # the buffer crosses the fork
626                for q in PARTS:
627                    removed[prep.chains[q][prep.s_px[q] < buffer_px - lo]] = True
628            out.append((p, scored, removed))
629    return out

The left-out blocks: (part, scored, removed) node masks.

Each part is cut into blocks of block_px px from the fork outwards (the fork belongs to the trunk's first block). A block's readings and those within buffer_px px of it are removed from the fit; only the block's own are scored. Near the fork the buffer reaches into the other parts.

Arguments:
  • prep: The prepared tree.
  • block_px: Block length along the part (px).
  • buffer_px: Readings this close to a block are left out of its fit too (px).
Returns:

(part, scored, removed) per block: the part's name and two boolean node masks.

def block_cv( prep: Prepared, grid: Sequence[tuple[float, float]] = ((0.01, 0.05), (0.01, 0.1), (0.01, 0.2), (0.01, 0.4), (0.02, 0.05), (0.02, 0.1), (0.02, 0.2), (0.02, 0.4), (0.04, 0.05), (0.04, 0.1), (0.04, 0.2), (0.04, 0.4), (0.08, 0.05), (0.08, 0.1), (0.08, 0.2), (0.08, 0.4), (0.16, 0.05), (0.16, 0.1), (0.16, 0.2), (0.16, 0.4)), base: BendParams = BendParams(spread=0.02, length=0.2, huber=1.345, tukey=4.685, iters=30, corr_px=7.0, min_noise=0.003, uncertain=0.5), block_px: float = 40, buffer_px: float = 10) -> dict[str, dict]: 
632def block_cv(prep: Prepared, grid: Sequence[tuple[float, float]] = GRID, base: BendParams = BendParams(),
633             block_px: float = BLOCK_PX, buffer_px: float = BUFFER_PX) -> dict[str, dict]:
634    """Left-out blocks' depth predicted by the plane and by each prior on ``grid``.
635
636    For each block (:func:`blocks`) the plane is fitted again without the removed readings, and the block's
637    readings are predicted by that plane (``h`` = 0) and by the bends fitted to the rest.
638
639    Args:
640        prep: The prepared tree.
641        grid: ``(τ, L)`` priors to try (m).
642        base: The other settings of the fit.
643        block_px: Block length (px).
644        buffer_px: Buffer around a block (px).
645
646    Returns:
647        ``{setting_key: {part: [sum of |error| (m), sum of error² (m²), readings]}}``, with ``"plane"`` first.
648    """
649    terms = prior_terms(prep)
650    settings = [replace(base, spread=0.0)] + [replace(base, spread=t, length=length) for t, length in grid]
651    out = {setting_key(s): {p: [0.0, 0.0, 0] for p in PARTS} for s in settings}
652    read = np.isfinite(prep.z_axis)
653    for part, scored, removed in blocks(prep, block_px, buffer_px):
654        target = scored & prep.anchor
655        keep = read & ~removed
656        if not target.any() or keep.sum() < 20:
657            continue
658        plane = fit_plane(prep.rays[keep] * prep.z_axis[keep, None])
659        if np.degrees(np.arccos(np.clip(-plane["normal"][2], -1, 1))) > MAX_TURN:
660            continue
661        d = np.where(prep.anchor, prep.z_axis - on_plane(prep.rays, plane)[:, 2], np.nan)
662        for s in settings:
663            h = fit_bends(prep, s, d=d, hold=removed, terms=terms)["h"]
664            e = d[target] - h[target]
665            acc = out[setting_key(s)][part]
666            acc[0] += float(np.abs(e).sum())
667            acc[1] += float((e ** 2).sum())
668            acc[2] += int(len(e))
669    return out

Left-out blocks' depth predicted by the plane and by each prior on grid.

For each block (blocks()) the plane is fitted again without the removed readings, and the block's readings are predicted by that plane (h = 0) and by the bends fitted to the rest.

Arguments:
  • prep: The prepared tree.
  • grid: (τ, L) priors to try (m).
  • base: The other settings of the fit.
  • block_px: Block length (px).
  • buffer_px: Buffer around a block (px).
Returns:

{setting_key: {part: [sum of |error| (m), sum of error² (m²), readings]}}, with "plane" first.

BEND_MEASURES = ('v_opening', 'trunk_out', 'left_bow', 'right_bow', 'left_tilt', 'right_tilt', 'left_tilt_whole', 'right_tilt_whole', 'fork_behind', 'trunk_out_max', 'left_out_max', 'right_out_max', 'trunk_out_rms', 'left_out_rms', 'right_out_rms', 'left_length', 'right_length', 'trunk_uncertain', 'left_uncertain', 'right_uncertain', 'trunk_anchors', 'left_anchors', 'right_anchors', 'sigma')

Columns of bend_measures(): degrees; *_bow, fork_behind, *_out_* and sigma in cm; lengths in m; *_uncertain and *_anchors shares of each part's points. *_tilt is a leader's line on its stretch out of the tree's plane, *_tilt_whole the line through all of it in view (degrees, positive: the upper end behind).

def bend_measures( prep: Prepared, h: numpy.ndarray, sd: numpy.ndarray | None = None, params: BendParams = BendParams(spread=0.02, length=0.2, huber=1.345, tukey=4.685, iters=30, corr_px=7.0, min_noise=0.003, uncertain=0.5), zoom: float = 1.0, shape: treeskel.shape.ShapeParams = ShapeParams(start=1.5, reach=16.0, trunk_reach=4.0, min_trunk=10.0, min_points=10, unit=16.5), sigma: float = nan) -> dict: 
687def bend_measures(prep: Prepared, h: np.ndarray, sd: np.ndarray | None = None, params: BendParams = BendParams(),
688                  zoom: float = 1.0, shape: ShapeParams = ShapeParams(), sigma: float = float("nan")) -> dict:
689    """One tree's measures of its 3D curves (see the module docstring).
690
691    Args:
692        prep: The tree (:func:`prepare`).
693        h: The bends (:func:`fit_bends`); zeros for the plane.
694        sd: Their posterior standard deviations (:func:`posterior_sd`), for the uncertain shares.
695        params: The prior (its ``spread`` and ``uncertain`` set what is uncertain).
696        zoom: Photo px per winter px, for the stretches (:data:`treeskel.shape.SUMMER_SCALE` in summer).
697        shape: The stretches of :mod:`treeskel.shape`: the trunk's top and each leader's line.
698        sigma: The fitted noise (m), reported in cm.
699
700    Returns:
701        :data:`BEND_MEASURES`, NaN where undefined (a leader or the trunk's top too short).
702    """
703    out = dict.fromkeys(BEND_MEASURES, float("nan"))
704    pts = bent_points(prep, h)
705    behind = behind_plane(prep, pts)
706    unit = UNIT_PX * zoom
707    out["fork_behind"] = float(behind[0] * 100)
708    out["sigma"] = float(sigma * 100)
709    for p in PARTS:
710        k = prep.nodes[p]
711        out[f"{p}_out_max"] = float(np.max(np.abs(behind[k])) * 100)
712        out[f"{p}_out_rms"] = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(behind[k] ** 2)) * 100)
713        out[f"{p}_anchors"] = float(np.mean(prep.anchor[k]))
714        if sd is not None and params.spread > 0:
715            out[f"{p}_uncertain"] = float(np.mean(sd[k] > params.uncertain * params.spread))
716    lines, parts = {}, {}
717    back = -prep.plane["normal"]                        # away from the camera, out of the tree's plane
718    for side in ("left", "right"):
719        k = prep.nodes[side]
720        out[f"{side}_length"] = float(arc_length(pts[k])[-1]) if len(k) > 1 else float("nan")
721        if len(k) >= shape.min_points:
722            out[f"{side}_tilt_whole"] = float(np.degrees(np.arcsin(np.clip(line_direction(pts[k]) @ back, -1, 1))))
723        m = stretch(prep.paths[side], unit, shape)
724        if m.sum() >= shape.min_points:
725            parts[side] = pts[k][m]
726            lines[side] = line_direction(parts[side])
727            out[f"{side}_tilt"] = float(np.degrees(np.arcsin(np.clip(lines[side] @ back, -1, 1))))
728    if len(lines) < 2:
729        return out
730    out["v_opening"] = angle(lines["left"], lines["right"])
731    normal = np.cross(lines["left"], lines["right"])
732    normal /= np.linalg.norm(normal)
733    if normal[2] > 0:                                   # face the camera, as the tree's plane
734        normal = -normal
735    for side, q in parts.items():
736        # The bow: the middle of the stretch against the middle of its chord, out of the V's plane.
737        sq = arc_length(q)
738        mid = np.array([np.interp(sq[-1] / 2, sq, q[:, j]) for j in range(3)])
739        out[f"{side}_bow"] = float(-(mid - (q[0] + q[-1]) / 2) @ normal * 100)
740    trunk = prep.paths["trunk"][::-1]                    # from the fork down
741    st = arc_length(trunk)
742    if len(trunk) > 1 and st[-1] >= shape.min_trunk:
743        top = st <= max(shape.trunk_reach * unit, shape.min_trunk)
744        if top.sum() >= 3:
745            down = line_direction(pts[prep.nodes["trunk"][::-1]][top])
746            out["trunk_out"] = float(np.degrees(np.arcsin(np.clip(-down @ normal, -1, 1))))
747    return out

One tree's measures of its 3D curves (see the module docstring).

Arguments:
  • prep: The tree (prepare()).
  • h: The bends (fit_bends()); zeros for the plane.
  • sd: Their posterior standard deviations (posterior_sd()), for the uncertain shares.
  • params: The prior (its spread and uncertain set what is uncertain).
  • zoom: Photo px per winter px, for the stretches (treeskel.shape.SUMMER_SCALE in summer).
  • shape: The stretches of treeskel.shape: the trunk's top and each leader's line.
  • sigma: The fitted noise (m), reported in cm.
Returns:

BEND_MEASURES, NaN where undefined (a leader or the trunk's top too short).

def mask_skeleton(mask: numpy.ndarray) -> dict | None: 
754def mask_skeleton(mask: np.ndarray) -> dict | None:
755    """A 256x256 summer mask's trunk and leaders in photo px, with each point's radius (photo px), or None.
756
757    Args:
758        mask: 256x256 boolean branch mask.
759
760    Returns:
761        ``{"paths", "radii"}`` per part, or None if no fork is found.
762    """
763    from scipy import ndimage as ndi
764
765    from treeskel.io import IMAGE_SHAPE, MASK_SHAPE
766    from treeskel.shape import mask_branches, mask_to_image
767
768    m = np.asarray(mask, bool)
769    br = mask_branches(m)
770    if br is None:
771        return None
772    k = IMAGE_SHAPE[0] / MASK_SHAPE[0]
773    half = ndi.distance_transform_edt(ndi.binary_fill_holes(m))
774    return {"paths": {p: mask_to_image(br[p]) for p in PARTS},
775            "radii": {p: np.maximum(half[br[p][:, 0], br[p][:, 1]], 0.5) * k for p in PARTS}}

A 256x256 summer mask's trunk and leaders in photo px, with each point's radius (photo px), or None.

Arguments:
  • mask: 256x256 boolean branch mask.
Returns:

{"paths", "radii"} per part, or None if no fork is found.

def cv_tree(job: tuple) -> dict: 
797def cv_tree(job: tuple) -> dict:
798    """Phase 1 for one tree (top-level for worker processes): the winter block cross-validation.
799
800    Args:
801        job: ``(record, clicks)``.
802
803    Returns:
804        ``{"tree", "row", "radii", "cv", "error"}``; ``cv`` as :func:`block_cv`, None if the plane failed.
805    """
806    rec, clicks = job
807    images, sk = winter_skeleton(rec, clicks)
808    out = {"tree": rec.tree_id, "row": rec.row, "radii": sk["radii"], "cv": None, "error": ""}
809    try:
810        out["cv"] = block_cv(prepare(sk["paths"], images["depth"], images["valid"], sk["radii"]))
811    except ValueError as e:
812        out["error"] = str(e)
813    return out

{"tree", "row", "radii", "cv", "error"}; cv as block_cv(), None if the plane failed.

def measure_tree(job: tuple) -> list[dict]: 
816def measure_tree(job: tuple) -> list[dict]:
817    """Phase 2 for one tree (top-level for worker processes): the chosen prior's 3D curves and measures.
818
819    Winter under every camera setting of :data:`treeskel.tree3d.SETTINGS`, with the plane and the bends,
820    and the block cross-validation again with :data:`BUFFER_PX` x 3 for the plane and the chosen prior;
821    winter with ridge readings only (``"winter ridges"``: the trunk where it stands clear of the ground) and
822    summer (the lined-up hand mask and the U-Net's mask, ridge readings only) under the main setting.
823
824    Args:
825        job: ``(record, clicks, winter radii, hand mask or None, U-Net mask or None, BendParams)``.
826
827    Returns:
828        One row per source, camera setting and model (``plane`` or ``bent``): the tree's 3D measures, or the
829        ``error`` that stopped the fit.
830    """
831    from treeskel.guided_gt import guided_gt
832    from treeskel.io import load_tree
833    from treeskel.shape import SUMMER_SCALE
834    from treeskel.tree3d import SETTINGS
835
836    rec, clicks, radii, hand, unet, params = job
837    images = load_tree(rec, "winter")
838    gt = guided_gt(images["rgb"], images["depth"], images["valid"], clicks)
839    winter = {"paths": {p: getattr(gt, p) for p in PARTS}, "radii": radii}
840    # Winter twice: every reading (the truth), and only the ridges, as summer (a check on the ground's depth).
841    sources = [("winter", winter, images, False, 1.0), ("winter ridges", winter, images, True, 1.0)]
842    summer = None
843    for name, mask in (("hand masks", hand), ("U-Net", unet)):
844        sk = mask_skeleton(mask) if mask is not None else None
845        if sk is not None:
846            summer = summer or load_tree(rec, "summer")
847            sources.append((name, sk, summer, True, SUMMER_SCALE))
848    rows = []
849    for name, sk, im, ridge, zoom in sources:
850        for setting, camera in (SETTINGS.items() if name == "winter" else [("main", SETTINGS["main"])]):
851            base = {"tree": rec.tree_id, "row": rec.row, "source": name, "setting": setting}
852            try:
853                prep = prepare(sk["paths"], im["depth"], im["valid"], sk["radii"], camera, ridge=ridge)
854            except ValueError as e:
855                rows.append({**base, "model": "bent", "error": str(e)})
856                continue
857            fit = fit_bends(prep, params)
858            sd = posterior_sd(fit)
859            rows.append({**base, "model": "plane", "error": "",
860                         **bend_measures(prep, np.zeros(len(fit["h"])), None, params, zoom)})
861            rows.append({**base, "model": "bent", "error": "",
862                         **bend_measures(prep, fit["h"], sd, params, zoom, sigma=fit["sigma"])})
863            if name == "winter" and setting == "main":
864                cv = block_cv(prep, grid=[(params.spread, params.length)], base=params, buffer_px=3 * BUFFER_PX)
865                for key, model in (("plane", "plane"), (setting_key(params), "bent")):
866                    acc = cv[key]
867                    n = sum(acc[p][2] for p in PARTS)
868                    rows[-2 if model == "plane" else -1]["cv_wide_mae"] = (
869                        sum(acc[p][0] for p in PARTS) / n * 100 if n else float("nan"))
870    return rows

Phase 2 for one tree (top-level for worker processes): the chosen prior's 3D curves and measures.

Winter under every camera setting of treeskel.tree3d.SETTINGS, with the plane and the bends, and the block cross-validation again with BUFFER_PX x 3 for the plane and the chosen prior; winter with ridge readings only ("winter ridges": the trunk where it stands clear of the ground) and summer (the lined-up hand mask and the U-Net's mask, ridge readings only) under the main setting.

Arguments:
  • job: (record, clicks, winter radii, hand mask or None, U-Net mask or None, BendParams).
Returns:

One row per source, camera setting and model (plane or bent): the tree's 3D measures, or the error that stopped the fit.

def pooled_mae( cv_rows: Sequence[dict], trees: set | None = None, parts: Sequence[str] = ('trunk', 'left', 'right')) -> dict[str, float]: 
895def pooled_mae(cv_rows: Sequence[dict], trees: set | None = None, parts: Sequence[str] = PARTS) -> dict[str, float]:
896    """Each setting's mean absolute error over all left-out readings of ``trees`` (all if None), in cm.
897
898    Args:
899        cv_rows: Phase 1's rows (:func:`cv_table`).
900        trees: Tree ids to pool (all if None).
901        parts: Parts to pool.
902
903    Returns:
904        ``{setting: MAE in cm}``.
905    """
906    tot: dict[str, list[float]] = {}
907    for r in cv_rows:
908        if (trees is None or r["tree"] in trees) and r["part"] in parts:
909            a = tot.setdefault(r["setting"], [0.0, 0])
910            a[0] += r["sum_abs"]
911            a[1] += r["n"]
912    return {k: a[0] / a[1] * 100 for k, a in tot.items() if a[1]}

def choose(cv_rows: Sequence[dict], trees: set | None = None) -> str: 
934def choose(cv_rows: Sequence[dict], trees: set | None = None) -> str:
935    """The rule fixed before the 449-tree run: the prior on :data:`GRID` with the smallest pooled mean
936    absolute error over the left-out blocks of ``trees`` (all if None).
937
938    Args:
939        cv_rows: Phase 1's rows (:func:`cv_table`).
940        trees: Tree ids to choose on (all if None).
941
942    Returns:
943        The chosen prior's :func:`setting_key`.
944    """
945    pooled = pooled_mae(cv_rows, trees)
946    return min((k for k in pooled if k != "plane"), key=pooled.get)

def params_of( key: str, base: BendParams = BendParams(spread=0.02, length=0.2, huber=1.345, tukey=4.685, iters=30, corr_px=7.0, min_noise=0.003, uncertain=0.5)) -> BendParams: 
949def params_of(key: str, base: BendParams = BendParams()) -> BendParams:
950    """The :class:`BendParams` a :func:`setting_key` names.
951
952    Args:
953        key: A :func:`setting_key`.
954        base: The other settings.
955
956    Returns:
957        The prior, ``spread`` 0 for ``"plane"``.
958    """
959    if key == "plane":
960        return replace(base, spread=0.0)
961    _, tau, _, length = key.split()
962    return replace(base, spread=float(tau) / 100, length=float(length) / 100)

The BendParams a setting_key() names.

  • base: The other settings.
Returns:

The prior, spread 0 for "plane".

def out_of_fold(cv_rows: Sequence[dict], fold_rows: Sequence[Sequence[int]]) -> dict: 
965def out_of_fold(cv_rows: Sequence[dict], fold_rows: Sequence[Sequence[int]]) -> dict:
966    """The bends against the plane with the prior chosen on the other folds' trees (row-grouped).
967
968    Args:
969        cv_rows: Phase 1's rows (:func:`cv_table`).
970        fold_rows: The rows of each cross-validation fold.
971
972    Returns:
973        ``{"chosen": [key per fold scored], "trees": {tree: (plane MAE, bent MAE)}}`` (cm); a fold with no
974        trees, or with no trees outside it, is skipped.
975    """
976    row_of = {r["tree"]: r["row"] for r in cv_rows}
977    plane = tree_mae(cv_rows, "plane")
978    out = {"chosen": [], "trees": {}}
979    for rows in fold_rows:
980        inside = {t for t, r in row_of.items() if r in rows}
981        if not inside or not set(row_of) - inside:          # nothing to score, or nothing to choose on
982            continue
983        key = choose(cv_rows, set(row_of) - inside)
984        out["chosen"].append(key)
985        bent = tree_mae([r for r in cv_rows if r["tree"] in inside], key)
986        for t in inside:
987            if t in bent and t in plane:
988                out["trees"][t] = (plane[t], bent[t])
989    return out

The bends against the plane with the prior chosen on the other folds' trees (row-grouped).

Arguments:
  • cv_rows: Phase 1's rows (cv_table()).
  • fold_rows: The rows of each cross-validation fold.
Returns:

{"chosen": [key per fold scored], "trees": {tree: (plane MAE, bent MAE)}} (cm); a fold with no trees, or with no trees outside it, is skipped.

SUMMER_MEASURES = ('trunk_out', 'left_bow', 'right_bow', 'v_opening')

The measures compared between the seasons, tree by tree.

def summer_against_winter(rows: Sequence[dict], source: str, measure: str) -> dict: 
1018def summer_against_winter(rows: Sequence[dict], source: str, measure: str) -> dict:
1019    """A summer source's bends and its plane against winter's bends, tree by tree, on one measure.
1020
1021    Args:
1022        rows: Phase 2's rows (:func:`measure_tree`).
1023        source: The summer source (``"hand masks"``, ``"U-Net"`` or ``"winter ridges"``).
1024        measure: The measure compared.
1025
1026    Returns:
1027        ``{"n", "median_bent", "median_plane", "bent_closer", "wilcoxon_p", "spearman"}``: the median
1028        ``|summer − winter|`` with the summer bends and with the summer plane, the share of trees where the
1029        bends are closer, the Wilcoxon p of the paired differences, and the rank correlation of the summer
1030        bends with winter's.
1031    """
1032    from scipy import stats
1033
1034    def get(src, model):
1035        """One source's and model's ``measure`` per tree (main setting, fitted, finite)."""
1036        return {r["tree"]: r[measure] for r in rows if r["source"] == src and r["setting"] == "main"
1037                and r["model"] == model and not r.get("error") and np.isfinite(r.get(measure, np.nan))}
1038
1039    w, b, p = get("winter", "bent"), get(source, "bent"), get(source, "plane")
1040    t = [k for k in w if k in b and k in p]
1041    if len(t) < 3:
1042        return {"n": len(t)}
1043    w_, b_, p_ = (np.array([m[k] for k in t]) for m in (w, b, p))
1044    eb, ep = np.abs(b_ - w_), np.abs(p_ - w_)
1045    d = ep - eb
1046    varied = np.std(b_) > 0 and np.std(w_) > 0
1047    return {"n": len(t), "median_bent": float(np.median(eb)), "median_plane": float(np.median(ep)),
1048            "bent_closer": float(np.mean(d > 0)),
1049            "wilcoxon_p": float(stats.wilcoxon(d).pvalue) if np.any(d != 0) else 1.0,
1050            "spearman": float(stats.spearmanr(w_, b_)[0]) if varied else None}

A summer source's bends and its plane against winter's bends, tree by tree, on one measure.

Arguments:
  • rows: Phase 2's rows (measure_tree()).
  • source: The summer source ("hand masks", "U-Net" or "winter ridges").
  • measure: The measure compared.
Returns:

{"n", "median_bent", "median_plane", "bent_closer", "wilcoxon_p", "spearman"}: the median |summer − winter| with the summer bends and with the summer plane, the share of trees where the bends are closer, the Wilcoxon p of the paired differences, and the rank correlation of the summer bends with winter's.

def summarise( cv_rows: Sequence[dict], rows: Sequence[dict], fold_rows: Sequence[Sequence[int]]) -> dict: 
1053def summarise(cv_rows: Sequence[dict], rows: Sequence[dict], fold_rows: Sequence[Sequence[int]]) -> dict:
1054    """The report: the cross-validation, winter's bends, their sensitivity, and summer against winter.
1055
1056    Args:
1057        cv_rows: Phase 1's rows (:func:`cv_table`).
1058        rows: Phase 2's rows (:func:`measure_tree`).
1059        fold_rows: The rows of each cross-validation fold.
1060
1061    Returns:
1062        The report (``report.json``).
1063    """
1064    from treeskel.tree3d import SETTINGS
1065
1066    chosen = choose(cv_rows)
1067    oof = out_of_fold(cv_rows, fold_rows)
1068    report = {"n_trees_cv": len({r["tree"] for r in cv_rows}), "grid": pooled_mae(cv_rows), "chosen": chosen,
1069              "parts": {p: {k: pooled_mae(cv_rows, parts=[p]).get(k) for k in ("plane", chosen)} for p in PARTS},
1070              "out_of_fold": {"chosen": oof["chosen"],
1071                              **_paired_better({t: v[0] for t, v in oof["trees"].items()},
1072                                               {t: v[1] for t, v in oof["trees"].items()})}}
1073
1074    def col(source, model, measure, setting="main"):
1075        """One source's, model's and setting's ``measure`` per tree (fitted, finite)."""
1076        return {r["tree"]: r[measure] for r in rows if r["source"] == source and r["setting"] == setting
1077                and r["model"] == model and not r.get("error") and np.isfinite(r.get(measure, np.nan))}
1078
1079    report["wide_buffer"] = _paired_better(col("winter", "plane", "cv_wide_mae"), col("winter", "bent", "cv_wide_mae"))
1080    bent = [r for r in rows if r["source"] == "winter" and r["setting"] == "main" and r["model"] == "bent"
1081            and not r.get("error")]
1082    report["winter"] = {k: _q([r[k] for r in bent]) for k in BEND_MEASURES}
1083    for side in ("left", "right"):
1084        report["winter"][f"{side}_bow_abs"] = _q([abs(r[f"{side}_bow"]) for r in bent])
1085    vb, vp = col("winter", "bent", "v_opening"), col("winter", "plane", "v_opening")
1086    report["winter"]["v_change"] = _q([vb[t] - vp[t] for t in vb if t in vp])
1087    for side in ("left", "right"):
1088        lb, lp = col("winter", "bent", f"{side}_length"), col("winter", "plane", f"{side}_length")
1089        report["winter"][f"{side}_length_change"] = _q([(lb[t] - lp[t]) * 100 for t in lb if t in lp])
1090    report["sensitivity"] = {}
1091    for setting in SETTINGS:
1092        sub = [r for r in rows if r["source"] == "winter" and r["setting"] == setting and r["model"] == "bent"
1093               and not r.get("error")]
1094        vb_, vp_ = col("winter", "bent", "v_opening", setting), col("winter", "plane", "v_opening", setting)
1095        report["sensitivity"][setting] = {
1096            "trunk_out": _q([r["trunk_out"] for r in sub])["median"],
1097            "bow_abs": _q([abs(r[f"{s}_bow"]) for r in sub for s in ("left", "right")])["median"],
1098            "out_max_leaders": _q([r[f"{s}_out_max"] for r in sub for s in ("left", "right")])["median"],
1099            "v_change": _q([vb_[t] - vp_[t] for t in vb_ if t in vp_])["median"]}
1100    ridges = summer_against_winter(rows, "winter ridges", "trunk_out")
1101    report["winter_ridges"] = {"trunk_out": _q(col("winter ridges", "bent", "trunk_out").values()),
1102                               "median_abs_diff": ridges.get("median_bent"), "spearman": ridges.get("spearman"),
1103                               "n": ridges.get("n", 0)}
1104    report["summer"] = {}
1105    for source in ("hand masks", "U-Net"):
1106        sub = [r for r in rows if r["source"] == source and r["model"] == "bent" and not r.get("error")]
1107        report["summer"][source] = {
1108            "n_trees": len(sub),
1109            "anchors": {p: _q([r[f"{p}_anchors"] for r in sub])["median"] for p in PARTS},
1110            "uncertain": {p: _q([r[f"{p}_uncertain"] for r in sub])["median"] for p in PARTS},
1111            "against_winter": {m: summer_against_winter(rows, source, m) for m in SUMMER_MEASURES}}
1112    # Failed planes under the main setting, and the winter ones under each other setting (whose medians above
1113    # leave them out).
1114    report["failed"] = {s: sorted({r["tree"] for r in rows if r["source"] == s and r["setting"] == "main"
1115                                   and r.get("error")}) for s in ("winter", "winter ridges", "hand masks", "U-Net")}
1116    report["failed_winter_by_setting"] = {
1117        setting: sorted({r["tree"] for r in rows if r["source"] == "winter" and r["setting"] == setting
1118                         and r.get("error")}) for setting in SETTINGS}
1119    return report

def report_lines(report: dict) -> list[str]: 
1126def report_lines(report: dict) -> list[str]:
1127    """The report as text.
1128
1129    Args:
1130        report: The report from :func:`summarise`.
1131
1132    Returns:
1133        The lines of text.
1134    """
1135    q = report["winter"]
1136    out = [f"Block cross-validation on {report['n_trees_cv']} development trees' winter depth "
1137           f"({BLOCK_PX} px blocks left out, {BUFFER_PX} px either side), mean absolute error of the left-out "
1138           "readings (cm):"]
1139    grid = report["grid"]
1140    out.append(f"  plane {grid['plane']:.2f}; best priors: " + ", ".join(
1141        f"{k} {grid[k]:.2f}" for k in sorted((k for k in grid if k != "plane"), key=grid.get)[:5]))
1142    out.append(f"  chosen (smallest pooled error): {report['chosen']}; by part, plane -> chosen: " + ", ".join(
1143        f"{p} {_f(v['plane'])} -> {_f(v[report['chosen']])}" for p, v in report["parts"].items()))
1144    o = report["out_of_fold"]
1145    if o.get("n", 0) >= 3:
1146        out.append(f"  out of fold (prior chosen on the other folds' rows: {', '.join(o['chosen'])}): bends better "
1147                   f"on {o['better']:.0%} of {o['n']} trees; median per tree {o['median_a']:.2f} -> "
1148                   f"{o['median_b']:.2f} cm (Wilcoxon p {o['wilcoxon_p']:.1e})")
1149    w = report["wide_buffer"]
1150    if w.get("n", 0) >= 3:
1151        out.append(f"  with {3 * BUFFER_PX} px buffers: bends better on {w['better']:.0%} of {w['n']} trees; median "
1152                   f"{w['median_a']:.2f} -> {w['median_b']:.2f} cm (Wilcoxon p {w['wilcoxon_p']:.1e})")
1153    out += ["", "Winter bends with the chosen prior (main camera setting), median [quartiles]:"]
1154    labels = (("trunk_out", "trunk out of the V's plane (deg, + = root behind)"),
1155              ("left_bow", "left leader's bow (cm, + = behind)"), ("right_bow", "right leader's bow (cm)"),
1156              ("left_bow_abs", "|left bow| (cm)"), ("right_bow_abs", "|right bow| (cm)"),
1157              ("left_tilt", "left leader's stretch out of the plane (deg, + = top behind)"),
1158              ("right_tilt", "right leader's stretch out of the plane (deg)"),
1159              ("left_tilt_whole", "left leader, whole, out of the plane (deg)"),
1160              ("right_tilt_whole", "right leader, whole, out of the plane (deg)"),
1161              ("fork_behind", "fork behind the plane (cm)"),
1162              ("trunk_out_max", "trunk's farthest from the plane (cm)"),
1163              ("left_out_max", "left leader's farthest (cm)"), ("right_out_max", "right leader's farthest (cm)"),
1164              ("v_change", "V opening, bends - plane (deg)"),
1165              ("left_length_change", "left leader longer by (cm)"),
1166              ("trunk_uncertain", "trunk points uncertain (share)"),
1167              ("left_uncertain", "left leader points uncertain"), ("sigma", "depth noise (cm)"))
1168    for k, label in labels:
1169        s = q.get(k)
1170        if s and s["n"]:
1171            out.append(f"  {label:62s} {s['median']:7.2f} [{s['q1']:.2f}, {s['q3']:.2f}]  (n {s['n']})")
1172    wr = report.get("winter_ridges", {})
1173    if wr.get("n", 0) >= 3:
1174        out.append(f"  with ridge readings only (the trunk clear of the ground): trunk out of the V's plane "
1175                   f"{wr['trunk_out']['median']:.2f} [{wr['trunk_out']['q1']:.2f}, {wr['trunk_out']['q3']:.2f}]; "
1176                   f"median |difference| from all readings {wr['median_abs_diff']:.2f} deg, rank correlation "
1177                   f"{_f(wr['spearman'])} (n {wr['n']})")
1178    out += ["", "Sensitivity (winter medians under each camera setting):",
1179            f"  {'setting':22s} {'trunk out':>10s} {'|bow|':>8s} {'leader max':>11s} {'V change':>9s}"]
1180    for setting, s in report["sensitivity"].items():
1181        out.append(f"  {setting:22s} {_f(s['trunk_out'], '.1f'):>10s} {_f(s['bow_abs']):>8s} "
1182                   f"{_f(s['out_max_leaders']):>11s} {_f(s['v_change']):>9s}")
1183    out += ["", "Summer (ridge readings only) against winter's bends, tree by tree: median |summer - winter| with "
1184                "the summer bends and with the summer plane; share of trees where the bends are closer; Wilcoxon p; "
1185                "rank correlation of the summer bends with winter's:"]
1186    for source, s in report["summer"].items():
1187        out.append(f"  {source} ({s['n_trees']} trees; readings that count, median share: " + ", ".join(
1188            f"{p} {_f(v, '.0%')}" for p, v in s["anchors"].items()) + "):")
1189        for m, a in s["against_winter"].items():
1190            if a.get("n", 0) >= 3:
1191                out.append(f"    {m:10s} n {a['n']:3d}  bends {a['median_bent']:6.2f}  plane {a['median_plane']:6.2f}  "
1192                           f"closer {a['bent_closer']:4.0%}  p {a['wilcoxon_p']:.1e}  rank {_f(a['spearman'])}")
1193    out += ["", "Failed planes under the main setting (turned more than "
1194            f"{MAX_TURN:g} deg, or too little depth): " + "; ".join(
1195                f"{s} {len(t)} ({', '.join(t) or 'none'})" for s, t in report["failed"].items())]
1196    other = {k: v for k, v in report.get("failed_winter_by_setting", {}).items() if k != "main"}
1197    if other:
1198        out.append("  winter under the other settings (left out of their medians): " + "; ".join(
1199            f"{k} {len(v)}" for k, v in other.items()))
1200    return out

The measures compared with winter's in the typical-shape run (--typical).

SUMMER_MODELS = ('plane', 'bent', 'typical', 'bent typical')

Summer's 3D curves in the typical-shape run: the plane; the bends with the plane as the prior's mean (as model3d until now); the typical winter shape alone, ignoring summer's readings; and the bends with the typical shape as the prior's mean.

def typical_winter(job: tuple) -> dict: 
1217def typical_winter(job: tuple) -> dict:
1218    """Pass 1 for one tree (top-level for worker processes): its winter bends, their profiles and measures.
1219
1220    Args:
1221        job: ``(record, clicks, BendParams)``.
1222
1223    Returns:
1224        ``{"tree", "row", "profiles": {part: values at STATIONS[part]}, "measures", "error"}``.
1225    """
1226    rec, clicks, params = job
1227    images, sk = winter_skeleton(rec, clicks)
1228    out = {"tree": rec.tree_id, "row": rec.row, "profiles": None, "measures": None, "error": ""}
1229    try:
1230        prep = prepare(sk["paths"], images["depth"], images["valid"], sk["radii"])
1231    except ValueError as e:
1232        out["error"] = str(e)
1233        return out
1234    fit = fit_bends(prep, params)
1235    out["profiles"] = {p: profile(prep, fit["h"], p) for p in PARTS}
1236    out["measures"] = bend_measures(prep, fit["h"], posterior_sd(fit), params, sigma=fit["sigma"])
1237    return out

Pass 1 for one tree (top-level for worker processes): its winter bends, their profiles and measures.

def typical_summer(job: tuple) -> list[dict]: 
1240def typical_summer(job: tuple) -> list[dict]:
1241    """Pass 2 for one tree (top-level for worker processes): summer's curves (:data:`SUMMER_MODELS`) and measures.
1242
1243    Args:
1244        job: ``(record, hand mask or None, U-Net mask or None, BendParams, typical shape)``; the shape learnt
1245            without the tree's own fold.
1246
1247    Returns:
1248        One row per summer source and model: the tree's measures, or the ``error`` that stopped the fit.
1249    """
1250    from treeskel.io import load_tree
1251    from treeskel.shape import SUMMER_SCALE
1252
1253    rec, hand, unet, params, shape = job
1254    rows, summer = [], None
1255    for name, mask in (("hand masks", hand), ("U-Net", unet)):
1256        sk = mask_skeleton(mask) if mask is not None else None
1257        if sk is None:
1258            continue
1259        summer = summer or load_tree(rec, "summer")
1260        base = {"tree": rec.tree_id, "row": rec.row, "source": name, "setting": "main"}
1261        try:
1262            prep = prepare(sk["paths"], summer["depth"], summer["valid"], sk["radii"], ridge=True)
1263        except ValueError as e:
1264            rows.append({**base, "model": "bent typical", "error": str(e)})
1265            continue
1266        terms = prior_terms(prep)
1267        mean = prior_mean(prep, shape)
1268        for model in SUMMER_MODELS:
1269            if model == "plane":
1270                h, sd, sigma = np.zeros(len(mean)), None, float("nan")
1271            elif model == "typical":
1272                h, sd, sigma = mean, None, float("nan")
1273            else:
1274                fit = fit_bends(prep, params, terms=terms, mean=mean if model == "bent typical" else None)
1275                h, sd, sigma = fit["h"], posterior_sd(fit), fit["sigma"]
1276            rows.append({**base, "model": model, "error": "",
1277                         **bend_measures(prep, h, sd, params, SUMMER_SCALE, sigma=sigma)})
1278    return rows

def fold_shapes( winter: Sequence[dict], fold_rows: Sequence[Sequence[int]], min_trees: int = 20) -> dict: 
1281def fold_shapes(winter: Sequence[dict], fold_rows: Sequence[Sequence[int]], min_trees: int = MIN_TREES) -> dict:
1282    """The typical shape from every tree, and for each fold from the other folds' trees only.
1283
1284    Args:
1285        winter: Pass 1's rows, with each tree's profiles.
1286        fold_rows: The rows of each fold.
1287        min_trees: As for :func:`typical_shape`.
1288
1289    Returns:
1290        ``{"all": shape, "folds": [shape per fold]}`` (:func:`typical_shape`).
1291    """
1292    ok = [w for w in winter if w["profiles"] is not None]
1293    return {"all": typical_shape([w["profiles"] for w in ok], min_trees),
1294            "folds": [typical_shape([w["profiles"] for w in ok if w["row"] not in rows], min_trees)
1295                      for rows in fold_rows]}

1300
